## ReportVersions

An abstract contract that defines the Data Streams report schemas (`ReportV1` through `ReportV13`).

[`ReportVersions`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-local/blob/v0.3.1/src/data-streams/ReportVersions.sol)

> **NOTE**
>
> These structs mirror the Data Streams report schemas. For the schema reference, see the [Data Streams report
> schemas](https://docs.chain.link/data-streams/reference/report-schema-overview).
> [`MockReportGenerator`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/mock-report-generator) inherits from this contract and
> generates signed reports for each version.

## Structs

### ReportV1

> **CAUTION: Deprecated**
>
> The v1 schema (early crypto report with block metadata) is deprecated; it is included for historical reference and
> backwards compatibility with legacy streams.

| Field                 | Type      | Description                                          |
| --------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| feedId                | `bytes32` | The stream ID the report has data for                |
| observationsTimestamp | `uint32`  | Observation timestamp in seconds                     |
| benchmarkPrice        | `int192`  | DON consensus median benchmark price                 |
| bid                   | `int192`  | Bid-side price estimate                              |
| ask                   | `int192`  | Ask-side price estimate                              |
| currentBlockNum       | `uint64`  | Current block number used by the report              |
| currentBlockHash      | `bytes32` | Current block hash used by the report                |
| validFromBlockNum     | `uint64`  | Earliest block number from which the report is valid |
| currentBlockTimestamp | `uint64`  | Current block timestamp in seconds                   |

### ReportV2

> **NOTE**
>
> Crypto streams schema. The `benchmarkPrice` value is carried to either 8 or 18 decimal places, depending on the
> stream.

| Field                 | Type      | Description                                                |
| --------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| feedId                | `bytes32` | The feed ID the report has data for                        |
| validFromTimestamp    | `uint32`  | Earliest timestamp for which price is applicable           |
| observationsTimestamp | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp for which price is applicable             |
| nativeFee             | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in the native token   |
| linkFee               | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in LINK               |
| expiresAt             | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp where the report can be verified on-chain |
| benchmarkPrice        | `int192`  | DON consensus median price                                 |

### ReportV3

> **NOTE**
>
> Crypto streams schema with bid/ask. The `price`, `bid`, and `ask` values are carried to either 8 or 18 decimal places,
> depending on the stream.

| Field                 | Type      | Description                                                                        |
| --------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| feedId                | `bytes32` | The stream ID the report has data for                                              |
| validFromTimestamp    | `uint32`  | Earliest timestamp for which price is applicable                                   |
| observationsTimestamp | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp for which price is applicable                                     |
| nativeFee             | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in the native token                           |
| linkFee               | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in LINK                                       |
| expiresAt             | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp where the report can be verified on-chain                         |
| price                 | `int192`  | DON consensus median price                                                         |
| bid                   | `int192`  | Simulated price impact of a buy order up to the X% depth of liquidity utilisation  |
| ask                   | `int192`  | Simulated price impact of a sell order up to the X% depth of liquidity utilisation |

### ReportV4

> **NOTE**
>
> RWA stream schema. The `price` value is carried to either 8 or 18 decimal places. `marketStatus` indicates whether the
> market is currently open: `0` (`Unknown`), `1` (`Closed`), `2` (`Open`).

| Field                 | Type      | Description                                                 |
| --------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| feedId                | `bytes32` | The stream ID the report has data for                       |
| validFromTimestamp    | `uint32`  | Earliest timestamp for which price is applicable            |
| observationsTimestamp | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp for which price is applicable              |
| nativeFee             | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in the native token    |
| linkFee               | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in LINK                |
| expiresAt             | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp where the report can be verified on-chain  |
| price                 | `int192`  | DON consensus median benchmark price                        |
| marketStatus          | `uint32`  | The DON's consensus on whether the market is currently open |

### ReportV5

> **NOTE**
>
> Rate report schema.

| Field                 | Type      | Description                                                |
| --------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| feedId                | `bytes32` | The stream ID the report has data for                      |
| validFromTimestamp    | `uint32`  | Earliest timestamp for which the report is applicable      |
| observationsTimestamp | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp for which the report is applicable        |
| nativeFee             | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in the native token   |
| linkFee               | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in LINK               |
| expiresAt             | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp where the report can be verified on-chain |
| rate                  | `int192`  | Reported rate value                                        |
| timestamp             | `uint32`  | Rate timestamp in seconds                                  |
| duration              | `uint32`  | Duration window in seconds                                 |

### ReportV6

> **NOTE**
>
> Multi-price report schema.

| Field                 | Type      | Description                                                |
| --------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| feedId                | `bytes32` | The stream ID the report has data for                      |
| validFromTimestamp    | `uint32`  | Earliest timestamp for which the report is applicable      |
| observationsTimestamp | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp for which the report is applicable        |
| nativeFee             | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in the native token   |
| linkFee               | `uint192` | Base cost to validate a transaction, in LINK               |
| expiresAt             | `uint32`  | Latest timestamp where the report can be verified on-chain |
| price                 | `int192`  | Primary price value                                        |
| price2                | `int192`  | Secondary price value                                      |
| price3                | `int192`  | Third price value                                          |
| price4                | `int192`  | Fourth price value                                         |
| price5                | `int192`  | Fifth price value                                          |

### ReportV7 through ReportV13

> **NOTE**
>
> `ReportV7` through `ReportV13` follow the same base layout (feed ID, validity timestamps, native and LINK fees,
> expiry) with schema-specific payload fields. See the [Data Streams report schema
> overview](https://docs.chain.link/data-streams/reference/report-schema-overview) for each schema's fields.

## WETH9

A contract that implements Wrapped Ether (WETH), allowing users to wrap and unwrap ETH.

[`WETH9`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-local/blob/v0.3.1/src/shared/WETH9.sol)

> **NOTE**
>
> This contract provides functionality to wrap ETH into WETH and unwrap WETH back to ETH, along with standard ERC20
> operations.

## Variables

### allowance

```solidity
mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public allowance
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Mapping of owner addresses to spender addresses to approved amounts.

### balanceOf

```solidity
mapping(address => uint256) public balanceOf
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Mapping of addresses to their WETH balances.

### decimals

```solidity
uint8 public decimals = 18
```

> **NOTE**
>
> The number of decimals used for WETH token amounts.

### name

```solidity
string public name = "Wrapped Ether"
```

> **NOTE**
>
> The name of the token.

### symbol

```solidity
string public symbol = "WETH"
```

> **NOTE**
>
> The symbol of the token.

## Events

### Approval

```solidity
event Approval(address indexed src, address indexed guy, uint256 wad)
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Emitted when an approval is set.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                         |
| --------- | --------- | ----------------------------------- |
| src       | `address` | The address giving the approval     |
| guy       | `address` | The address receiving the approval  |
| wad       | `uint256` | The amount of tokens being approved |

### Deposit

```solidity
event Deposit(address indexed dst, uint256 wad)
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Emitted when ETH is wrapped to WETH.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                     |
| --------- | --------- | ------------------------------- |
| dst       | `address` | The address receiving the WETH  |
| wad       | `uint256` | The amount of ETH being wrapped |

### Transfer

```solidity
event Transfer(address indexed src, address indexed dst, uint256 wad)
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Emitted when tokens are transferred.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                            |
| --------- | --------- | -------------------------------------- |
| src       | `address` | The address sending the tokens         |
| dst       | `address` | The address receiving the tokens       |
| wad       | `uint256` | The amount of tokens being transferred |

### Withdrawal

```solidity
event Withdrawal(address indexed src, uint256 wad)
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Emitted when WETH is unwrapped to ETH.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                        |
| --------- | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
| src       | `address` | The address unwrapping the WETH    |
| wad       | `uint256` | The amount of WETH being unwrapped |

## Functions

### approve

Approves another address to spend tokens.

```solidity
function approve(address guy, uint256 wad) public returns (bool)
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Sets the allowance that a spender has to access the caller's tokens.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                     |
| --------- | --------- | ------------------------------- |
| guy       | `address` | The address to approve          |
| wad       | `uint256` | The amount of tokens to approve |

#### Returns

| Parameter | Type   | Description         |
| --------- | ------ | ------------------- |
| (unnamed) | `bool` | Always returns true |

### deposit

Deposits ETH to receive WETH.

```solidity
function deposit() external payable
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Allows users to deposit ETH and receive WETH tokens.

### totalSupply

Gets the total supply of WETH.

```solidity
function totalSupply() public view returns (uint256)
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Returns the total amount of ETH held by this contract.

#### Returns

| Parameter | Type      | Description              |
| --------- | --------- | ------------------------ |
| (unnamed) | `uint256` | The total supply of WETH |

### transfer

Transfers tokens to another address.

```solidity
function transfer(address dst, uint256 wad) public returns (bool)
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Transfers tokens from the caller to another address.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                      |
| --------- | --------- | -------------------------------- |
| dst       | `address` | The recipient address            |
| wad       | `uint256` | The amount of tokens to transfer |

#### Returns

| Parameter | Type   | Description                           |
| --------- | ------ | ------------------------------------- |
| (unnamed) | `bool` | Returns true if the transfer succeeds |

### transferFrom

Transfers tokens from one address to another.

```solidity
function transferFrom(address src, address dst, uint256 wad) public returns (bool)
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Transfers tokens between addresses, respecting allowances.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                      |
| --------- | --------- | -------------------------------- |
| src       | `address` | The source address               |
| dst       | `address` | The destination address          |
| wad       | `uint256` | The amount of tokens to transfer |

#### Returns

| Parameter | Type   | Description                           |
| --------- | ------ | ------------------------------------- |
| (unnamed) | `bool` | Returns true if the transfer succeeds |

#### Possible Reverts

- Reverts if the source address has insufficient balance
- Reverts if the caller has insufficient allowance (unless caller is source or has maximum allowance)

### withdraw

Withdraws ETH by unwrapping WETH.

```solidity
function withdraw(uint256 wad) external
```

> **NOTE**
>
> Allows users to withdraw ETH by burning WETH tokens.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                  |
| --------- | --------- | ---------------------------- |
| wad       | `uint256` | The amount of WETH to unwrap |

#### Possible Reverts

- Reverts if the caller has insufficient WETH balance

# CCT - getCCIPAdmin() token with Burn and Mint Pool in forked environments
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-burn-and-mint-fork

> **NOTE: Integrate Chainlink Local into your project**
>
> ### npm
>
> If you use [NPM](https://www.npmjs.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> npm install @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### yarn
>
> If you use [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> yarn add @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### foundry
>
> If you use [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/):
>
> ```shell
> forge install smartcontractkit/chainlink-local@v0.3.1
> ```
>
> and then set remappings to: `@chainlink/local/=lib/chainlink-local/` in either `remappings.txt` or `foundry.toml` file
>
> ### RemixIDE
>
> Import the `CCIPLocalSimulator` contract from the `@chainlink/local` package:
>
> ```solidity
> import {CCIPLocalSimulator} from "@chainlink/local@0.3.1/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulator.sol";
> ```

This tutorial walks you through testing the procedure of enabling your own tokens in CCIP 2.0, using the [CCIP Foundry Starter Kit](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry)'s Example 06 (CCT 01). You will deploy a `CrossChainToken` (a CCT-compatible ERC-20 that exposes `getCCIPAdmin()`) with a Burn & Mint pool on forks of *Ethereum Sepolia* and *Polygon Amoy*, register it in the live TokenAdminRegistry, link the pools, opt them into Fast Transfers, and send a transfer across the CCIP 2.0 lane with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork` routing the message.

The kit runs this exact flow as a fork test (`test/fork/Example06.fork.t.sol`), so every step below is verified against pinned forks of the live testnets.

## Prerequisites

> **NOTE: Prerequisites**
>
> Familiarize yourself with the [CCT standard](/ccip/concepts/cross-chain-token/overview) and [CCIP
> architecture](/ccip/concepts/architecture/overview) before proceeding with this tutorial. Complete the [Foundry forked environments guide](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/local-simulator-fork) first: it covers the fork profile, `evm_version = "cancun"`, Foundry >= 1.5.1 and the RPC setup.

Before we start with this guide, let's recap parts of the CCT standard that we will need for it.

### Requirements for Cross-Chain Tokens

Before enabling an ERC20-compatible token in CCIP, it's important to understand the requirements it must fulfill to integrate with CCIP.

- **Recommended permissionless token administrator address registration methods**: A token can use either of these supported function signatures to register permissionlessly:
  - `owner()`: This function returns the token contract owner's address.
  - `getCCIPAdmin()`: This function returns the token administrator's address and is recommended for new tokens, as it allows for abstraction of the CCIP Token Administrator role from other common roles, like `owner()`.

    > **NOTE**
    >
    > In the event that these functions are not available, registration can be performed by submitting a form
    > [here](https://chain.link/ccip-contact).

- **Requirements for CCIP token transfers**: The token's smart contract must meet minimum requirements to integrate with CCIP.
  - **Burn & Mint Requirements**:
    - The token smart contract must have the following functions:
      - `mint(address account, uint256 amount)`: This function is used to mint the `amount` of tokens to a given `account` on the destination blockchain.
      - `burn(uint256 amount)`: This function is used to burn the `amount` of tokens on the source blockchain.
      - `decimals()`: Returns the token's number of decimals.
      - `balanceOf(address account)`: Returns the current token balance of the specified `account`.
      - `burnFrom(address account, uint256 amount)`: This function burns a specified number of tokens from the provided account on the source blockchain. **Note**: This is an optional function. We generally recommend using the `burn` function, but if you use a tokenPool that calls `burnFrom`, your token contract will need to implement this function.
    - On the source and destination blockchains, the token contract must support granting mint and burn permissions. The token developers or another role (such as the token administrator) will grant these permissions to the token pool.

If you don't have an existing token, the kit deploys a `CrossChainToken` for you: a `BaseERC20` with `getCCIPAdmin()`, mint and burn roles, and a pre-mint, configured in one constructor call.

### Understanding the Procedure

It is also important first to understand the overall procedure for enabling your tokens in CCIP. This procedure involves deploying tokens and token pools, registering administrative roles, and configuring token pools to enable secure token transfers using CCIP. The steps in the diagram below highlight the flow of actions needed to enable a token for cross-chain transfers. Whether you're working with an Externally Owned Account (EOA) or a **Smart Account** (such as one using a multisig scheme), the overall logic remains the same. You'll follow the same process to enable cross-chain token transfers, configure pools, and register administrative roles.

The diagram below outlines the entire process:

![Process for enabling a token in CCIP.](/images/ccip/CCIP_enabled_tokens_flowchart.jpg)

## Before You Begin

1. **Install Foundry >= 1.5.1**: If you haven't already, follow the instructions in the [Foundry documentation](https://book.getfoundry.sh/getting-started/installation).

2. **Clone the starter kit** and initialize the submodules one level deep:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry
   cd ccip-starter-kit-foundry
   git submodule update --init
   ```

3. **Set up your environment**: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in archive-capable RPC endpoints for both chains:

   ```bash
   ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL=<ethereum_sepolia_rpc_url>
   POLYGON_AMOY_RPC_URL=<polygon_amoy_rpc_url>
   ```

4. **Import a keystore account** for script execution:

   ```bash
   cast wallet import myAccount --interactive
   ```

   This tutorial assumes `--account myAccount`.

> **NOTE: Optimizer is required for CCT pool deployment**
>
> `BurnMintTokenPool` can exceed the EVM max code size if compiled without the optimizer. The kit includes a dedicated
> CCT profile in `foundry.toml` (`[profile.cct]` with `optimizer = true, optimizer_runs = 200`). Use
> `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct` in all deployment commands of this tutorial.

## Step 1: Deploy the token and pool on Ethereum Sepolia (source)

Run the `DeployCCTBurnMintTokenAndPool` script. It deploys the `CrossChainToken` (name `TestToken`, symbol `TEST`, 18 decimals, `1_000_000e18` pre-mint to the broadcaster, `100_000_000e18` max supply), the BurnMint pool, grants the pool mint and burn roles on the token, registers the token admin via `getCCIPAdmin()`, accepts the admin role, and sets the pool in the TokenAdminRegistry:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example06.s.sol:DeployCCTBurnMintTokenAndPool \
  --rpc-url ethereumSepolia \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,address,address,address)" \
  <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADMIN_REGISTRY> \
  <SEPOLIA_REGISTRY_MODULE_OWNER_CUSTOM> \
  <SEPOLIA_ARM_PROXY> \
  <SEPOLIA_ROUTER>
```

Read the four addresses from the [CCIP Directory](/ccip/directory/testnet) (or from `Register.getNetworkDetails(11155111)`). Save from the logs:

- `<SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS>`
- `<SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS>`

## Step 2: Deploy the token and pool on Polygon Amoy (destination)

Repeat the same script on Amoy:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example06.s.sol:DeployCCTBurnMintTokenAndPool \
  --rpc-url polygonAmoy \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,address,address,address)" \
  <AMOY_TOKEN_ADMIN_REGISTRY> \
  <AMOY_REGISTRY_MODULE_OWNER_CUSTOM> \
  <AMOY_ARM_PROXY> \
  <AMOY_ROUTER>
```

Save `<AMOY_TOKEN_ADDRESS>` and `<AMOY_POOL_ADDRESS>`.

## Step 3: Configure the Sepolia pool with the Amoy remote

The `Example06` script links a pool to its remote chain: it sets the remote token, the remote pool, and (in this example) a disabled rate limiter. Re-running it for the same remote chain selector replaces the existing config:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example06.s.sol:Example06 \
  --rpc-url ethereumSepolia \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,uint64,address,address)" \
  <SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS> \
  <AMOY_CHAIN_SELECTOR> \
  <AMOY_TOKEN_ADDRESS> \
  <AMOY_POOL_ADDRESS>
```

## Step 4: Configure the Amoy pool with the Sepolia remote

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example06.s.sol:Example06 \
  --rpc-url polygonAmoy \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,uint64,address,address)" \
  <AMOY_POOL_ADDRESS> \
  <SEPOLIA_CHAIN_SELECTOR> \
  <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS> \
  <SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS>
```

## Step 5: (Optional) Enable Fast Transfers on both pools

New pools allow full finality only (`0x00000000`): every transfer waits for full finality. To opt a pool into Faster Than Finality, set its allowed finality config to a minimum block depth:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example06.s.sol:Example06SetPoolAllowedFinalityConfig \
  --rpc-url ethereumSepolia \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,bytes4)" \
  <SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS> \
  <ALLOWED_FINALITY_CONFIG>
```

Repeat on Amoy with `--rpc-url polygonAmoy` and `<AMOY_POOL_ADDRESS>`. `0x00000000` disables Faster Than Finality; values `0x00000001`-`0x0000ffff` set the minimum block depth. Read each pool back with the `Example06GetPoolAllowedFinalityConfig` script.

Before an FTF send, check the lane's finality gates (pool, executor and CCV settings) with the read-only `Example06CheckFinalityGates` script. A `getFee` quote alone does not prove `ccipSend` will succeed for a non-`IPoolV2` pool.

## Step 6: Send the transfer across the lane

Send with default finality (`blockConfirmations = 0`):

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example06.s.sol:SendCCTTokenWithExtraArgsV3DefaultFinality \
  --rpc-url ethereumSepolia \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,uint64,address,address,uint256,uint32,address)" \
  <SEPOLIA_ROUTER> \
  <AMOY_CHAIN_SELECTOR> \
  <RECEIVER_ON_AMOY> \
  <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS> \
  <AMOUNT> \
  <GAS_LIMIT> \
  <FEE_TOKEN_ADDRESS>
```

Parameter notes:

- `<AMOUNT>` uses token decimals (`1e18` is 1 token for an 18-decimal token).
- `<GAS_LIMIT>`: set to `0` for a token-only transfer to an EOA receiver.
- `<FEE_TOKEN_ADDRESS>`: the LINK token address on Sepolia to pay in LINK, or `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` to pay in native.

For the Faster Than Finality version (after Step 5), use `SendCCTTokenWithExtraArgsV3CustomFinality` with the same signature plus `<BLOCK_CONFIRMATIONS_GT_ZERO>`.

The script logs the message ID. Monitor the message on [CCIP Explorer](https://ccip.chain.link).

## Run the same flow as a fork test

The kit's `test/fork/Example06.fork.t.sol` runs this entire procedure against pinned forks of the live testnets, with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork` routing each message to the Amoy OffRamp. The core of the test:

```solidity
// Deploy on both forks through the real script
(sepoliaToken, sepoliaPool) = _deploy(sepoliaFork, sepolia);
(amoyToken, amoyPool) = _deploy(amoyFork, amoy);

// Link the pools through the real script
vm.selectFork(sepoliaFork);
configureLaneScript.run(sepoliaPool, amoy.chainSelector, amoyToken, amoyPool);
vm.selectFork(amoyFork);
configureLaneScript.run(amoyPool, sepolia.chainSelector, sepoliaToken, sepoliaPool);

// Send on Sepolia and route to the Amoy OffRamp
vm.selectFork(sepoliaFork);
sendDefaultFinality.run(
    sepolia.routerAddress, amoy.chainSelector, receiver, sepoliaToken, TRANSFER_AMOUNT,
    EOA_RECEIVER_GAS_LIMIT, address(0)
);
simulator.switchChainAndRouteMessage(amoyFork);

// Burn & Mint: supply shrinks on the source and grows on the destination
assertEq(_balanceOnFork(amoyFork, amoyToken, receiver), TRANSFER_AMOUNT);
assertEq(_supplyOnFork(amoyFork, amoyToken), destinationSupplyBefore + TRANSFER_AMOUNT);
```

Run it with:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=fork forge test --match-contract Example06ForkTest -j 1
```

The fork test also covers the Faster Than Finality gates: it asserts the pool rejects block-depth requests until `setAllowedFinalityConfig` opts it in, then finds the smallest depth the live lane accepts and delivers the transfer at that depth.

## Verify the result on the live testnets

After the transfer finalizes, verify the registration and the lane mapping:

```bash
cast call <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADMIN_REGISTRY> "getPool(address)(address)" <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS> --rpc-url ethereumSepolia
cast call <SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS> "getRemoteToken(uint64)(bytes)" <AMOY_CHAIN_SELECTOR> --rpc-url ethereumSepolia
cast call <SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS> "getRemotePools(uint64)(bytes[])" <AMOY_CHAIN_SELECTOR> --rpc-url ethereumSepolia
```

Verify the Burn & Mint behavior (burn on source, mint on destination):

```bash
cast call <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS> "balanceOf(address)(uint256)" <SOURCE_EOA_ADDRESS> --rpc-url ethereumSepolia
cast call <AMOY_TOKEN_ADDRESS> "balanceOf(address)(uint256)" <RECEIVER_ON_AMOY> --rpc-url polygonAmoy
cast call <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS> "totalSupply()(uint256)" --rpc-url ethereumSepolia
cast call <AMOY_TOKEN_ADDRESS> "totalSupply()(uint256)" --rpc-url polygonAmoy
```

## Next steps

- For the Lock & Release flow (with a lock box and liquidity funding), read the [CCT lock and release tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-lock-and-release-fork).
- For the full CCT registration procedure against live testnets (not forks), read [Register a new Burn and Mint token from an EOA](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-foundry).

# CCT - getCCIPAdmin() token with Lock and Release Pool in forked environments
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-lock-and-release-fork

> **NOTE: Integrate Chainlink Local into your project**
>
> ### npm

> If you use [NPM](https://www.npmjs.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM

> ```shell
> npm install @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### yarn
>
> If you use [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> yarn add @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### foundry
>
> If you use [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/):
>
> ```shell
> forge install smartcontractkit/chainlink-local@v0.3.1
> ```
>
> and then set remappings to: `@chainlink/local/=lib/chainlink-local/` in either `remappings.txt` or `foundry.toml` file
>
> ### RemixIDE
>
> Import the `CCIPLocalSimulator` contract from the `@chainlink/local` package:
>
> ```solidity
> import {CCIPLocalSimulator} from "@chainlink/local@0.3.1/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulator.sol";
> ```

This tutorial walks you through testing the Lock & Release flow for enabling your own tokens in CCIP 2.0, using the [CCIP Foundry Starter Kit](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry)'s Example 07 (CCT 02). You will deploy a `CrossChainToken` (a CCT-compatible ERC-20 that exposes `getCCIPAdmin()`) with an `ERC20LockBox` and a Lock & Release pool on forks of *Ethereum Sepolia* and *Polygon Amoy*, fund the destination lock box with liquidity, and send a transfer across the CCIP 2.0 lane with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork` routing the message.

The kit runs this exact flow as a fork test (`test/fork/Example07.fork.t.sol`), so every step below is verified against pinned forks of the live testnets.

## Prerequisites

> **NOTE: Prerequisites**
>
> Familiarize yourself with the [CCT standard](/ccip/concepts/cross-chain-token/overview) and [CCIP
> architecture](/ccip/concepts/architecture/overview) before proceeding with this tutorial. Complete the [CCT burn and
> mint tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-burn-and-mint-fork) first: it covers the kit setup, the
> keystore, the CCT profile and the deployment scripts shared by this tutorial.

Before we start with this guide, let's recap parts of the CCT standard that we will need for it.

### Requirements for Cross-Chain Tokens

Before enabling an ERC20-compatible token in CCIP, it's important to understand the requirements it must fulfill to integrate with CCIP.

- **Recommended permissionless token administrator address registration methods**: A token can use either of these supported function signatures to register permissionlessly:
  - `owner()`: This function returns the token contract owner's address.
  - `getCCIPAdmin()`: This function returns the token administrator's address and is recommended for new tokens, as it allows for abstraction of the CCIP Token Administrator role from other common roles, like `owner()`.

    > **NOTE**
    >
    > In the event that these functions are not available, registration can be performed by submitting a form
    > [here](https://chain.link/ccip-contact).

- **Requirements for CCIP token transfers**: The token's smart contract must meet minimum requirements to integrate with CCIP.
  - **Lock & Release Requirements**:
    - The token smart contract must have the following functions:
      - `decimals()`: Returns the token's number of decimals.
      - `balanceOf(address account)`: Returns the current token balance of the specified `account`.
    - On the destination blockchain, the token contract must support granting mint and burn permissions. The token developers or another role (such as the token administrator) will grant these permissions to the token pool.

In the Lock & Release flow, the source pool locks the tokens in its lock box and the destination pool releases tokens from its own lock box liquidity. Nothing is burned or minted: the total supply stays constant on every chain, and the destination lock box must hold enough liquidity before a transfer can execute.

### Understanding the Procedure

It is also important first to understand the overall procedure for enabling your tokens in CCIP. This procedure involves deploying tokens and token pools, registering administrative roles, and configuring token pools to enable secure token transfers using CCIP. The steps in the diagram below highlight the flow of actions needed to enable a token for cross-chain transfers. Whether you're working with an Externally Owned Account (EOA) or a **Smart Account** (such as one using a multisig scheme), the overall logic remains the same. You'll follow the same process to enable cross-chain token transfers, configure pools, and register administrative roles.

The diagram below outlines the entire process:

![Process for enabling a token in CCIP.](/images/ccip/CCIP_enabled_tokens_flowchart.jpg)

## Before You Begin

Complete the [CCT burn and mint tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-burn-and-mint-fork) prerequisites: clone the kit, initialize the submodules, set `ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` and `POLYGON_AMOY_RPC_URL` in `.env`, and import a keystore account (`cast wallet import myAccount --interactive`). This tutorial assumes `--account myAccount` and `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct` for the deployment commands.

## Step 1: Deploy the token, lock box and pool on Ethereum Sepolia (source)

Run the `DeployCCTLockReleaseTokenAndPool` script. It deploys the `CrossChainToken` (name `TestToken`, symbol `TEST`, 18 decimals, `1_000_000e18` pre-mint to the broadcaster, `100_000_000e18` max supply), the `ERC20LockBox`, and the Lock & Release pool (wired to the lock box), authorizes the pool as a lock box caller, registers the token admin via `getCCIPAdmin()`, accepts the admin role, and sets the pool in the TokenAdminRegistry:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example07.s.sol:DeployCCTLockReleaseTokenAndPool \
  --rpc-url ethereumSepolia \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,address,address,address)" \
  <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADMIN_REGISTRY> \
  <SEPOLIA_REGISTRY_MODULE_OWNER_CUSTOM> \
  <SEPOLIA_ARM_PROXY> \
  <SEPOLIA_ROUTER>
```

Read the four addresses from the [CCIP Directory](/ccip/directory/testnet). Save from the logs:

- `<SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS>`
- `<SEPOLIA_LOCKBOX_ADDRESS>`
- `<SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS>`

## Step 2: Deploy the token, lock box and pool on Polygon Amoy (destination)

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example07.s.sol:DeployCCTLockReleaseTokenAndPool \
  --rpc-url polygonAmoy \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,address,address,address)" \
  <AMOY_TOKEN_ADMIN_REGISTRY> \
  <AMOY_REGISTRY_MODULE_OWNER_CUSTOM> \
  <AMOY_ARM_PROXY> \
  <AMOY_ROUTER>
```

Save `<AMOY_TOKEN_ADDRESS>`, `<AMOY_LOCKBOX_ADDRESS>` and `<AMOY_POOL_ADDRESS>`.

## Step 3: Configure each pool with the other chain as its remote

The `Example07` script links a pool to its remote chain (remote token, remote pool, disabled rate limiter in this example). Run it on both chains:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example07.s.sol:Example07 \
  --rpc-url ethereumSepolia \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,uint64,address,address)" \
  <SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS> \
  <AMOY_CHAIN_SELECTOR> \
  <AMOY_TOKEN_ADDRESS> \
  <AMOY_POOL_ADDRESS>
```

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example07.s.sol:Example07 \
  --rpc-url polygonAmoy \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,uint64,address,address)" \
  <AMOY_POOL_ADDRESS> \
  <SEPOLIA_CHAIN_SELECTOR> \
  <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS> \
  <SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS>
```

## Step 4: Fund the destination lock box with liquidity

Before a Sepolia → Amoy transfer can execute, the Amoy lock box must hold tokens to release. Fund it with the `FundCCTLockBoxLiquidity` script:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example07.s.sol:FundCCTLockBoxLiquidity \
  --rpc-url polygonAmoy \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,address,uint256)" \
  <AMOY_TOKEN_ADDRESS> \
  <AMOY_LOCKBOX_ADDRESS> \
  <DESTINATION_LIQUIDITY>
```

> **CAUTION: Fund the destination lock box first**
>
> Without liquidity the destination OffRamp cannot release the tokens and the message fails on the destination chain.
> The kit's fork test asserts exactly this failure path: without lock box funding, `switchChainAndRouteMessage` reverts
> with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork__MessageExecutionFailed`.

## Step 5: Send the transfer across the lane

Send with default finality using the shared CCT sender script:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=cct forge script script/examples/Example06.s.sol:SendCCTTokenWithExtraArgsV3DefaultFinality \
  --rpc-url ethereumSepolia \
  --account myAccount \
  --broadcast \
  --sig "run(address,uint64,address,address,uint256,uint32,address)" \
  <SEPOLIA_ROUTER> \
  <AMOY_CHAIN_SELECTOR> \
  <RECEIVER_ON_AMOY> \
  <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS> \
  <AMOUNT> \
  <GAS_LIMIT> \
  <FEE_TOKEN_ADDRESS>
```

- `<GAS_LIMIT>`: set to `0` for a token-only transfer to an EOA receiver.
- `<FEE_TOKEN_ADDRESS>`: the LINK token address on Sepolia to pay in LINK, or `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` to pay in native.

The script logs the message ID. Monitor the message on [CCIP Explorer](https://ccip.chain.link).

## Run the same flow as a fork test

The kit's `test/fork/Example07.fork.t.sol` runs this entire procedure against pinned forks of the live testnets. The core of the test:

```solidity
// Deploy on both forks through the real script
(sepoliaToken, sepoliaLockBox, sepoliaPool) = _deploy(sepoliaFork, sepolia);
(amoyToken, amoyLockBox, amoyPool) = _deploy(amoyFork, amoy);

// Link the pools through the real script
vm.selectFork(sepoliaFork);
configureLaneScript.run(sepoliaPool, amoy.chainSelector, amoyToken, amoyPool);
vm.selectFork(amoyFork);
configureLaneScript.run(amoyPool, sepolia.chainSelector, sepoliaToken, sepoliaPool);

// Fund the destination lock box first
vm.selectFork(amoyFork);
fundLockBoxScript.run(amoyToken, amoyLockBox, DESTINATION_LIQUIDITY);

// Send on Sepolia and route to the Amoy OffRamp
_sendDefaultFinalityAndRoute(sepoliaToken, TRANSFER_AMOUNT);

// Lock & Release: supply is unchanged on both chains
assertEq(_balanceOnFork(sepoliaFork, sepoliaToken, sepoliaLockBox), TRANSFER_AMOUNT);
assertEq(_supplyOnFork(sepoliaFork, sepoliaToken), PREMINT);
assertEq(_balanceOnFork(amoyFork, amoyToken, receiver), TRANSFER_AMOUNT);
assertEq(_balanceOnFork(amoyFork, amoyToken, amoyLockBox), DESTINATION_LIQUIDITY - TRANSFER_AMOUNT);
assertEq(_supplyOnFork(amoyFork, amoyToken), PREMINT);
```

Run it with:

```bash
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=fork forge test --match-contract Example07ForkTest -j 1
```

The fork test also asserts the empty-lock-box failure: it sends without funding the Amoy lock box and expects the routing call to revert with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork__MessageExecutionFailed`, which is the strict-routing surface of the destination OffRamp's recorded failure.

## Verify the result on the live testnets

After the transfer finalizes, verify the registration, the lane mapping and the Lock & Release behavior:

```bash
cast call <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADMIN_REGISTRY> "getPool(address)(address)" <SEPOLIA_TOKEN_ADDRESS> --rpc-url ethereumSepolia
cast call <SEPOLIA_POOL_ADDRESS> "getRemoteToken(uint64)(bytes)" <AMOY_CHAIN_SELECTOR> --rpc-url ethereumSepolia
cast call <SEPOLIA_LOCKBOX_ADDRESS> "balanceOf(address)(uint256)" <SEPOLIA_LOCKBOX_ADDRESS> --rpc-url ethereumSepolia
cast call <AMOY_TOKEN_ADDRESS> "balanceOf(address)(uint256)" <RECEIVER_ON_AMOY> --rpc-url polygonAmoy
cast call <AMOY_LOCKBOX_ADDRESS> "balanceOf(address)(uint256)" <AMOY_LOCKBOX_ADDRESS> --rpc-url polygonAmoy
```

The total supply on each chain is unchanged: nothing was burned or minted.

## Next steps

- For the Burn & Mint flow, read the [CCT burn and mint tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-burn-and-mint-fork).
- For pool hooks, pool-based CCVs and policy engines, see the kit's Examples 08-10 (`AdvancedPoolHooks`).
- For the full CCT registration procedure against live testnets (not forks), read [Register a new Lock and Mint token from an EOA](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-foundry).

# Sending data to a receiver with CCV config in your Foundry project
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/data-messages-receiver-ccv-config

> **NOTE: Integrate Chainlink Local into your project**
>
> ### npm
>
> If you use [NPM](https://www.npmjs.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> npm install @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### yarn
>
> If you use [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> yarn add @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### foundry
>
> If you use [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/):
>
> ```shell
> forge install smartcontractkit/chainlink-local@v0.3.1
> ```
>
> and then set remappings to: `@chainlink/local/=lib/chainlink-local/` in either `remappings.txt` or `foundry.toml` file
>
> ### RemixIDE
>
> Import the `CCIPLocalSimulator` contract from the `@chainlink/local` package:
>
> ```solidity
> import {CCIPLocalSimulator} from "@chainlink/local@0.3.1/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulator.sol";
> ```

This guide walks you through the CCIP 2.0 receiver-side finality rules in local mode, using the [CCIP Foundry Starter Kit](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry)'s Example 02. You will send a data-only message to a `BasicMessageReceiverWithCCVs` contract with Fast Transfers, and see the local router reject it when the requested block confirmations fall below the receiver's minimum block depth.

The Example 01 guide covers a token-only transfer to an EOA, which is exactly the case that skips the receiver finality check. This guide covers the opposite case: a message with data and a receiver contract, where the local router reads the receiver's `getCCVsAndFinalityConfig` and enforces its allowed finality, reproducing the CCIP 2.0 OffRamp check. Read [CCIP 2.0 behavior in local mode](/chainlink-local/learn/ccip-v2-local) for the full rule list.

## Prerequisites

Complete the [Foundry local simulator guide](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/local-simulator) first: it covers cloning the kit, initializing the submodules, and the `LocalSimulatorTest` setup this guide builds on.

## Test data messages to a receiver with CCV config

The test file `Example02.t.sol` is located in the `./test` directory. It runs the real Example 02 scripts (`script/examples/Example02.s.sol`) against the Chainlink Local simulator. The file contains eight test cases:

1. **Deploy**: The deploy script wires the receiver to the router and the broadcaster owns it.
2. **Deliver above the minimum depth**: A Fast Transfer with confirmations above the receiver's `minBlockDepth` is delivered.
3. **Deliver at the minimum depth**: Confirmations equal to `minBlockDepth` are also delivered.
4. **Deliver with a CCV config applied**: A receiver with required and optional CCVs still gates on `minBlockDepth`.
5. **Revert below the minimum depth**: Confirmations below `minBlockDepth` revert with `FinalityCodec.InvalidRequestedFinality`.
6. **Revert when the minimum depth is unset**: Without a configured depth, the receiver accepts finalized messages only.
7. **Argument validation**: The `SetBasicMessageReceiverWithCCVsMinBlockDepth` script rejects a zero source chain selector.
8. **Send-time validation**: The send script requires `blockConfirmations > 0`, so every send in this file is a Fast Transfer.

In your terminal, run the following command to execute the test:

```shell
forge test --match-contract Example02Test
```

Example output:

```text
$ forge test --match-contract Example02Test
[⠊] Compiling...
No files changed, compilation skipped

Ran 8 tests for test/Example02.t.sol:Example02Test
[PASS] test_deliversMessageWhenConfirmationsAreAtLeastMinBlockDepth() (gas: 2033236)
[PASS] test_deliversMessageWhenConfirmationsEqualMinBlockDepth() (gas: 1993766)
[PASS] test_deliversMessageWhenReceiverHasCCVConfigApplied() (gas: 3418578)
[PASS] test_deployScriptWiresReceiverToRouterAndBroadcasterOwnsIt() (gas: 17951)
[PASS] test_revertsWhenConfirmationsAreBelowMinBlockDepth() (gas: 1835829)
[PASS] test_revertsWhenMinBlockDepthIsUnsetSoOnlyFullFinalityIsAccepted() (gas: 1233516)
[PASS] test_sendScriptRequiresNonZeroBlockConfirmations() (gas: 41304)
[PASS] test_setMinBlockDepthScriptRejectsZeroSourceChainSelector() (gas: 572902)
Suite result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 3.21ms (3.83ms CPU time)

Ran 1 test suite in 6.65ms (3.21ms CPU time): 8 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (8 total tests)
```

## Examine the code

### The receiver contract

`src/BasicMessageReceiverWithCCVs.sol` extends `BasicMessageReceiver` with a per-source-chain CCV and finality policy. Two settings matter for this guide:

- `setMinBlockDepth(sourceChainSelector, minBlockDepth)`: the minimum block depth the receiver accepts for Fast Transfers from that chain. `0` means the receiver requires default finality (fully finalized messages only).
- `getCCVsAndFinalityConfig(sourceChainSelector, sender)`: the CCIP 2.0 receiver interface the OffRamp calls for every message that is not a token-only transfer. The kit's receiver returns its stored CCV config and encodes `minBlockDepth` as the allowed finality with `FinalityCodec._encodeBlockDepth`.

### Setup

The `setUp()` function deploys the receiver through the kit's deploy script, so the test exercises the same deployment path the book's live-testnet flow uses:

```solidity
function setUp() public override {
    super.setUp();
    example = new Example02();
    receiver = BasicMessageReceiverWithCCVs(new DeployBasicMessageReceiverWithCCVs().run(address(router)));
}
```

The helper functions wrap the two scripts the test drives:

```solidity
function _setMinBlockDepth(uint16 minBlockDepth) internal {
    new SetBasicMessageReceiverWithCCVsMinBlockDepth().run(address(receiver), chainSelector, minBlockDepth);
}

function _send(uint16 blockConfirmations) internal returns (bytes32) {
    return example.run(
        address(router), chainSelector, address(receiver), MESSAGE_TEXT, GAS_LIMIT, blockConfirmations, address(0)
    );
}
```

The constants used:

```solidity
string internal constant MESSAGE_TEXT = "Hello CCIP 2.0";
uint32 internal constant GAS_LIMIT = 200_000;
```

`GAS_LIMIT` must be `> 0`: the receiver has a `ccipReceive` callback to execute, unlike the EOA receiver of Example 01.

### Deliver when confirmations meet the minimum depth

`test_deliversMessageWhenConfirmationsAreAtLeastMinBlockDepth` sets the receiver's minimum depth to `3` and sends with `5` confirmations:

```solidity
_setMinBlockDepth(3);

bytes32 messageId = _send(5);

assertEq(receiver.latestMessageId(), messageId);
assertEq(receiver.latestSourceChainSelector(), chainSelector);
assertEq(receiver.latestSender(), broadcaster);
assertEq(receiver.latestMessage(), abi.encode(MESSAGE_TEXT));
```

Inside the send, the local router parses the `ExtraArgsV3` requested finality, sees the message has data (not a token-only transfer), and calls the receiver's `getCCVsAndFinalityConfig`. The receiver's allowed finality is `FinalityCodec._encodeBlockDepth(3)`; the requested `5` is at least that, so the message is delivered synchronously and the assertions read the receiver's stored state directly.

`test_deliversMessageWhenConfirmationsEqualMinBlockDepth` sends with exactly `3` confirmations and passes: the check is inclusive.

### Revert when confirmations fall below the minimum depth

`test_revertsWhenConfirmationsAreBelowMinBlockDepth` sends with `2` confirmations against a minimum depth of `3`. The local router rejects the send with the same error the production OffRamp records, and no tokens or data move:

```solidity
_setMinBlockDepth(3);

vm.expectRevert(
    abi.encodeWithSelector(
        FinalityCodec.InvalidRequestedFinality.selector,
        FinalityCodec._encodeBlockDepth(2),
        FinalityCodec._encodeBlockDepth(3)
    )
);
_send(2);
```

The error carries both sides of the comparison: the requested finality (`2` block confirmations) and the allowed finality (the receiver's minimum depth `3`).

`test_revertsWhenMinBlockDepthIsUnsetSoOnlyFullFinalityIsAccepted` shows the default: with no depth configured, the receiver's allowed finality is `FinalityCodec.WAIT_FOR_FINALITY_FLAG`, so any Fast Transfer request reverts:

```solidity
vm.expectRevert(
    abi.encodeWithSelector(
        FinalityCodec.InvalidRequestedFinality.selector,
        FinalityCodec._encodeBlockDepth(1),
        FinalityCodec.WAIT_FOR_FINALITY_FLAG
    )
);
_send(1);
```

A message with `blockConfirmations = 0` (default finality) would still be delivered in this state, but the send script requires `> 0`, so this file always sends Fast Transfers.

### Deliver with a CCV config applied

`test_deliversMessageWhenReceiverHasCCVConfigApplied` configures the receiver with required and optional CCVs through `applyCCVConfigUpdates`, then verifies the finality gate still applies on top:

```solidity
address[] memory required = new address[](1);
required[0] = makeAddr("requiredCCV");
address[] memory optional = new address[](2);
optional[0] = makeAddr("optionalCCV1");
optional[1] = makeAddr("optionalCCV2");
BasicMessageReceiverWithCCVs.CCVConfigArgs[] memory configs =
    new BasicMessageReceiverWithCCVs.CCVConfigArgs[](1);
configs[0] = BasicMessageReceiverWithCCVs.CCVConfigArgs({
    requiredCCVs: required, optionalCCVs: optional, sourceChainSelector: chainSelector, optionalThreshold: 1
});
vm.prank(broadcaster);
receiver.applyCCVConfigUpdates(configs);
_setMinBlockDepth(3);
```

Local mode has no CCV verifiers, so it cannot check quorum. It does validate the config itself (duplicate CCVs, `optionalThreshold` beyond the optional list length) the same way the OffRamp does, so a receiver configured this way is accepted by the router-side validation and keeps gating on the minimum block depth. The test then asserts the same `InvalidRequestedFinality` revert for a `2`-confirmation send.

## Run the same flow on a live testnet

The kit's book chapter lists the script commands for the live-testnet flow: deploy the receiver on the destination chain, set its minimum block depth for your source chain, then send the data message from the source chain. See the [Example 02 chapter](https://smartcontractkit.github.io/ccip-starter-kit-foundry/examples/example02-hello-world-to-basic-message-receiver.html) of the kit's book.

## Next steps

- `Example03.t.sol` combines this receiver-side gating with a token transfer (data + tokens in one message).
- To see the receiver finality rules enforced by the real OffRamp instead of the local router, read the [forked environments guide](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/local-simulator-fork).
- For an index of every kit example and where its topic is documented, read the [CCIP starter kit examples map](/chainlink-local/learn/starter-kit-examples).

# Using the Chainlink Local Simulator to fork mainnets
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/forking-mainnets

> **NOTE: Integrate Chainlink Local into your project**
>
> ### npm
>
> If you use [NPM](https://www.npmjs.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> npm install @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### yarn
>
> If you use [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> yarn add @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### foundry
>
> If you use [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/):
>
> ```shell
> forge install smartcontractkit/chainlink-local@v0.3.1
> ```
>
> and then set remappings to: `@chainlink/local/=lib/chainlink-local/` in either `remappings.txt` or `foundry.toml` file
>
> ### RemixIDE
>
> Import the `CCIPLocalSimulator` contract from the `@chainlink/local` package:
>
> ```solidity
> import {CCIPLocalSimulator} from "@chainlink/local@0.3.1/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulator.sol";
> ```

This guide explains how to use the Chainlink Local Simulator to test cross-chain transactions in forked mainnet environments using Foundry. You'll use the `Register.sol` contract to read the network details of the chains you fork, and `setNetworkDetails` to add or override details when a chain is not in `Register` or its values have changed.

Fork routing supports every CCIP era: pre-1.6, 1.6 and CCIP 2.0 (CCV-based) lanes. If the mainnet lane you fork runs CCIP 2.0 through a dedicated router, read it with [`getCCIPV2RouterAddress`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#getccipv2routeraddress) or set it with [`setCCIPV2RouterAddress`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#setccipv2routeraddress), and send through that router. Messages sent through either router are routed by `switchChainAndRouteMessage`.

## Understanding Network Registration

The `Register.sol` smart contract contains pre-configured details for 134 chains, mainnets included, to accelerate cross-chain transaction simulations in Foundry. `getNetworkDetails` returns an all-zero struct for a chain ID that is not in `Register`; use `setNetworkDetails` to add it.

> **NOTE: Best Practice**
>
> Always verify contract addresses from `Register.sol` against the official [CCIP Directory](/ccip/directory/mainnet) to
> ensure you're using the correct network details.

Here's an example of how to verify network details for a test network such as Sepolia:

```solidity
pragma solidity ^0.8.0;

import { Test, console } from "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {
    CCIPLocalSimulatorFork,
    Register
} from "@chainlink/local/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulatorFork.sol"

contract ExampleTest is Test {
    CCIPLocalSimulatorFork public ccipLocalSimulatorFork;
    uint256 public ethSepoliaFork;
    Register.NetworkDetails public ethSepoliaNetworkDetails;

    function setUp() public {
        // Create a fork of the Sepolia network
        string memory SEPOLIA_RPC_URL = vm.envString("SEPOLIA_RPC_URL");
        ethSepoliaFork = vm.createFork(SEPOLIA_RPC_URL);

        // Initialize the CCIP simulator
        ccipLocalSimulatorFork = new CCIPLocalSimulatorFork();
        vm.makePersistent(address(ccipLocalSimulatorFork));

        // Select and verify the fork
        vm.selectFork(ethSepoliaFork);
        assertEq(block.chainid, 11155111);

        // Verify network details match the CCIP Directory
        ethSepoliaNetworkDetails = ccipLocalSimulatorFork.getNetworkDetails(block.chainid);
        assertEq(ethSepoliaNetworkDetails.chainSelector, 16015286601757825753);
        assertEq(ethSepoliaNetworkDetails.routerAddress, 0x0BF3dE8c5D3e8A2B34D2BEeB17ABfCeBaf363A59);
    }
}
```

## Working with Mainnet Forks

The Chainlink Local Simulator supports any forked environment where CCIP contracts exist. Mainnet details are in `Register`, so forking a mainnet lane needs no extra configuration.

Chainlink Local runs this exact flow as an e2e test: [`CCIPv2MainnetEthereumArbitrumFork.t.sol`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-local/blob/v0.3.1/test/e2e/ccip/CCIPv2MainnetEthereumArbitrumFork.t.sol) sends a data-only message across the *Ethereum* → *Arbitrum One* mainnet lane, a CCIP 2.0 lane, and needs only `ETHEREUM_MAINNET_RPC_URL` and `ARBITRUM_MAINNET_RPC_URL`. The core of the test:

```solidity
function setUp() public {
    s_ethereumFork = vm.createSelectFork(vm.envString("ETHEREUM_MAINNET_RPC_URL"));
    s_arbitrumFork = vm.createFork(vm.envString("ARBITRUM_MAINNET_RPC_URL"));

    s_forkSimulator = new CCIPLocalSimulatorFork();
    vm.makePersistent(address(s_forkSimulator));
    s_encoder = new EncodeExtraArgsOffchain();
    vm.makePersistent(address(s_encoder));

    // Read the network details of both chains from Register
    vm.selectFork(s_arbitrumFork);
    s_arbitrum = s_forkSimulator.getNetworkDetails(block.chainid);
    vm.selectFork(s_ethereumFork);
    s_ethereum = s_forkSimulator.getNetworkDetails(block.chainid);

    // Fail fast if the lane is not CCIP 2.0 at the forked block
    address onRamp = IRouterOnRamp(s_ethereum.routerAddress).getOnRamp(s_arbitrum.chainSelector);
    assertEq(ITypeAndVersion(onRamp).typeAndVersion(), "OnRamp 2.0.0", "Ethereum -> Arbitrum is not CCIP 2.0");

    s_alice = makeAddr("alice");
    vm.deal(s_alice, 10 ether);
}

function test_mainnet_message_ethereumToArbitrum_fork() external {
    // Deploy a receiver on the destination chain
    vm.selectFork(s_arbitrumFork);
    BasicMessageReceiver receiver = new BasicMessageReceiver(s_arbitrum.routerAddress);

    // Send an ExtraArgsV3 message with default finality through the Ethereum router, paying in native
    bytes memory payload = bytes("Hello mainnet CCIP 2.0");
    bytes32 messageId = _send(
        address(receiver),
        payload,
        new Client.EVMTokenAmount[](0),
        s_encoder.encodeV3Basic(200_000, FinalityCodec.WAIT_FOR_FINALITY_FLAG)
    );

    // Route the message to the Arbitrum OffRamp
    s_forkSimulator.switchChainAndRouteMessage(s_arbitrumFork);

    // Verify the message arrived
    vm.selectFork(s_arbitrumFork);
    assertEq(receiver.latestMessageId(), messageId);
    assertEq(receiver.latestSourceChainSelector(), s_ethereum.chainSelector);
    assertEq(receiver.latestSender(), s_alice);
    assertEq(receiver.latestMessage(), payload);
}
```

The `_send` helper builds the `Client.EVM2AnyMessage` with the given extraArgs, quotes the fee, and calls `ccipSend` as `alice` paying in native. The test's receiver and encoder are chainlink-local test contracts (`src/test/ccip/`, not shipped in the npm package); for your own project, the [CCIP Foundry Starter Kit](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry) ships a receiver (`src/BasicMessageReceiver.sol`) and an extraArgs encoder (`script/EncodeExtraArgsOffchain.s.sol`).

**Code explanation**:

- **Network Setup**: The `setUp()` function creates forks of both Ethereum and Arbitrum One mainnets, initializes the CCIP simulator, and reads both chains' details from `Register` with no manual configuration.
- **Lane check**: The `OnRamp 2.0.0` assertion fails the test early if the lane is not CCIP 2.0 at the forked block, for example after a chain upgrade.
- **Message Transfer**: The test deploys the receiver on the destination fork, sends an `ExtraArgsV3` message with default finality (`FinalityCodec.WAIT_FOR_FINALITY_FLAG`) through the source router, and routes it with [`switchChainAndRouteMessage()`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#switchchainandroutemessage), which executes it on the destination OffRamp. Contracts created in a fork test are per-fork: make them persistent with `vm.makePersistent` before using them on another fork.

## Add or override network details with setNetworkDetails

Use [`setNetworkDetails()`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#setnetworkdetails) when a chain is not in `Register` (it returns an all-zero struct) or when a value has changed from the built-in one, for example after a router upgrade. The details are keyed by the **chain ID**, not the fork ID:

```solidity
ccipLocalSimulatorFork.setNetworkDetails(
  137, // Polygon mainnet chain ID
  Register.NetworkDetails({
    chainSelector: 4051577828743386545,
    routerAddress: 0x849c5ED5a80F5B408Dd4969b78c2C8fdf0565Bfe,
    linkAddress: 0xb0897686c545045aFc77CF20eC7A532E3120E0F1,
    wrappedNativeAddress: 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270,
    ccipBnMAddress: address(0), // not needed for this test
    ccipLnMAddress: address(0), // not needed for this test
    rmnProxyAddress: 0xf1ceAa46D8d13Cac9fC38aaEF3d3d14754C5A9c2,
    registryModuleOwnerCustomAddress: 0xc751E86208F0F8aF2d5CD0e29716cA7AD98B5eF5,
    tokenAdminRegistryAddress: 0x00F027eA6D0fb03256A15E9182B2B9227A4931d8
  })
);
```

The values above are the built-in `Register` entry for Polygon mainnet, shown as an example of the full struct. Check the [CCIP Directory](/ccip/directory/mainnet) for the current values of the chain you are configuring. Parameters not needed for messaging can be set to `address(0)`.

After this configuration, you can simulate cross-chain messages between any forks, enabling thorough testing of your cross-chain applications in a local environment.

### Using the Chainlink Local Simulator in your Foundry project

> If you use [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/):
>
> ```shell
> forge install smartcontractkit/chainlink-local@v0.3.1
> ```
>
> and then set remappings to: `@chainlink/local/=lib/chainlink-local/` in either `remappings.txt` or `foundry.toml` file
>
> ### RemixIDE
>
> Import the `CCIPLocalSimulator` contract from the `@chainlink/local` package:
>
> ```solidity
> import {CCIPLocalSimulator} from "@chainlink/local@0.3.1/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulator.sol";
> ```

You can use Chainlink Local to run CCIP 2.0 in forked environments within your Foundry project. To get started quickly, you will use the
[CCIP Foundry Starter Kit](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry). The kit's `test/fork` directory contains fork tests for the CCT examples (`Example06`-`Example10`), which run the real example scripts against pinned forks of *Ethereum Sepolia* and *Polygon Amoy* (a live CCIP 2.0 lane) and route each message to the destination OffRamp with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork`.

`CCIPLocalSimulatorFork` routes messages on forked networks for every CCIP era: pre-1.6 (`EVM2EVMOnRamp`), 1.6 and CCIP 2.0 (CCV-based lanes, which live testnet lanes run today). On CCIP 2.0 lanes the destination OffRamp selects the CCVs and executes the message (`V2VerificationMode.OFFRAMP_DERIVED`, the default); CCV attestations are simulated with a synthetic no-op verifier.

## Prerequisites

This guide assumes that you are familiar with the guide [Using the Chainlink Local Simulator in your Foundry project](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/local-simulator).
If not, please get familiar with it and run all the prerequisites.

Fork tests have two requirements beyond the no-fork setup:

1. **Foundry >= 1.5.1.**
2. **`evm_version = "cancun"` or later for the fork tests.** Deployed CCIP 2.0 contracts use Cancun opcodes; compiling with `paris` fails with `EvmError: NotActivated`. Use a fork-only profile so your deployed bytecode is not affected. The kit's `foundry.toml` does exactly this:

   ```toml
   [profile.fork]
   optimizer = true
   optimizer_runs = 200
   no_match_path = 'test/none/**'
   match_path = 'test/fork/**'
   ```

   `evm_version = 'cancun'` is set at the top level of the kit's `foundry.toml`.

Set up an `.env` file (or export the variables) with the fork RPC URLs. The kit needs archive-capable endpoints for both chains:

- `ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL`: The RPC URL for the Ethereum Sepolia testnet. You can sign up for a personal endpoint from [Alchemy](https://www.alchemy.com/),
  [Infura](https://www.infura.io/), or another node provider service.
- `POLYGON_AMOY_RPC_URL`: The RPC URL for the Polygon Amoy testnet, from the same providers.

## Test a CCT transfer across a CCIP 2.0 lane

You will run the fork test for Example 06 (CCT 01: `CrossChainToken` + BurnMint pool). The test file `Example06.fork.t.sol` is located in the `./test/fork` directory. It deploys a custom token and pool on both forks, registers them in the live TokenAdminRegistry, links the pools, and sends token transfers across the Sepolia → Amoy CCIP 2.0 lane. The file contains seven test cases, including:

1. **Deploy**: Creates the token and pool on both chains and registers them.
2. **Configure lane**: Sets the remote token and pool on each pool.
3. **Send with default finality**: Burns on the source and mints on the destination.
4. **Send with Faster Than Finality**: Reverts until both pools opt in, then delivers after the pools opt in.

In your terminal, run the following command to execute the test:

```shell
FOUNDRY_PROFILE=fork forge test --match-contract Example06ForkTest -j 1
```

Example output:

```text
$ FOUNDRY_PROFILE=fork forge test --match-contract Example06ForkTest -j 1
Ran 7 tests for test/fork/Example06.fork.t.sol:Example06ForkTest
[PASS] test_checkFinalityGates_findsRegisteredPool() (gas: 3066525)
[PASS] test_configureLane_rerunReplacesExistingConfig() (gas: 942262)
[PASS] test_configureLane_setsRemoteTokenAndPool() (gas: 747587)
[PASS] test_deploy_createsTokenAndPoolAndRegistersThem() (gas: 240027)
[PASS] test_send_defaultFinalityBurnsOnSourceAndMintsOnDestination() (gas: 2510920)
[PASS] test_send_fasterThanFinalityDeliversAfterPoolsOptIn() (gas: 3481610)
[PASS] test_send_fasterThanFinalityRevertsUntilPoolOptsIn() (gas: 1444822)
Suite result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 2.42s (15.51ms CPU time)

Ran 1 test suite in 2.42s (2.42s CPU time): 7 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (7 total tests)
```

## Examine the code

### Setup

The shared base contract `test/fork/utils/CCTForkTest.sol` sets up both forks and the simulator. To route messages across forks, the test needs:

- A fork of the source chain (Ethereum Sepolia) and the destination chain (Polygon Amoy)
- The network details (router, registry, RMN proxy addresses) for both chains
- The fork simulator, made persistent so it can route across forks
- A sender account (the broadcaster) and a receiver account

The `setUp()` function is invoked before each test case:

1. Create the forks. Both are pinned to a committed block (`DEFAULT_SEPOLIA_FORK_BLOCK`, `DEFAULT_AMOY_FORK_BLOCK`) so a fresh clone runs the same chain state. Override the pins per run with the `ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_FORK_BLOCK` / `POLYGON_AMOY_FORK_BLOCK` environment variables:

   ```solidity
   sepoliaFork =
       vm.createSelectFork("ethereumSepolia", vm.envOr("ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_FORK_BLOCK", DEFAULT_SEPOLIA_FORK_BLOCK));
   amoyFork = vm.createFork("polygonAmoy", vm.envOr("POLYGON_AMOY_FORK_BLOCK", DEFAULT_AMOY_FORK_BLOCK));
   ```

2. Initialize the [fork Chainlink Local simulator](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#cciplocalsimulatorfork) and make it persistent. The simulator must be created on a fork and be persistent so it can route across forks:

   ```solidity
   simulator = new CCIPLocalSimulatorFork();
   vm.makePersistent(address(simulator));
   ```

3. Read the network details for both chains with [`getNetworkDetails`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#getnetworkdetails). [`Register.NetworkDetails`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/register#networkdetails) stores the chain selector, router address, LINK address, wrapped native address, CCIP test tokens, RMN proxy, registry module and token admin registry addresses:

   ```solidity
   sepolia = simulator.getNetworkDetails(block.chainid);
   vm.selectFork(amoyFork);
   amoy = simulator.getNetworkDetails(block.chainid);
   ```

4. Fund the broadcaster on both forks and verify the lane is the CCIP 2.0 lane the test expects. The test fails with a clear message if the pinned block or the lane is not what it describes:

   ```solidity
   vm.selectFork(sepoliaFork);
   vm.deal(broadcaster, 100 ether);
   vm.selectFork(amoyFork);
   vm.deal(broadcaster, 100 ether);
   vm.selectFork(sepoliaFork);

   address onRamp = IRouterOnRampView(sepolia.routerAddress).getOnRamp(amoy.chainSelector);
   assertTrue(onRamp != address(0), "Sepolia router has no OnRamp for Amoy at the pinned block");
   assertEq(ITypeAndVersionView(onRamp).typeAndVersion(), "OnRamp 2.0.0", "Sepolia -> Amoy is not a CCIP 2.0 lane");
   ```

5. Contracts or scripts created in a fork test are per-fork: make them persistent before using them on another fork:

   ```solidity
   sendDefaultFinality = SendCCTTokenWithExtraArgsV3DefaultFinality(
       _persistent(address(new SendCCTTokenWithExtraArgsV3DefaultFinality()))
   );
   ```

### Send and route the message

The `_sendDefaultFinalityAndRoute` helper shows the two-step flow used by every fork test:

1. On the source fork, run the send script. It builds an `ExtraArgsV3` message with `blockConfirmations = 0` (default finality) and calls `ccipSend` through the Sepolia router:

   ```solidity
   vm.selectFork(sepoliaFork);
   sendDefaultFinality.run(
       sepolia.routerAddress, amoy.chainSelector, receiver, token, amount, EOA_RECEIVER_GAS_LIMIT, address(0)
   );
   ```

2. Call [`switchChainAndRouteMessage`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#switchchainandroutemessage) to switch to the destination fork and route the message. The simulator reads the recorded logs, finds the `CCIPMessageSent` event, and executes the message on the Amoy OffRamp. The active fork is Amoy when the call returns:

   ```solidity
   simulator.switchChainAndRouteMessage(amoyFork);
   ```

Routing is strict by default: `switchChainAndRouteMessage` reverts with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork__MessageNotRouted(messageId, reason)` when a captured message cannot be routed to any of the given forks, and with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork__MessageExecutionFailed(messageId, reason)` (the decoded revert data) when it does not execute successfully. Call [`setStrictRouting(false)`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#setstrictrouting) to record failures instead and read them with [`getMessageStatus`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork#getmessagestatus).

The Example 07 fork test (`test_send_failsToExecuteWhenDestinationLockBoxIsEmpty`) shows the strict-routing failure path: it sends a Lock & Release transfer without funding the destination lock box, so the OffRamp cannot release the tokens, and expects the routing call to revert:

```solidity
vm.expectPartialRevert(CCIPLocalSimulatorFork.CCIPLocalSimulatorFork__MessageExecutionFailed.selector);
simulator.switchChainAndRouteMessage(amoyFork);
```

### Faster Than Finality across the lane

The `test_send_fasterThanFinalityDeliversAfterPoolsOptIn` test case shows the CCIP 2.0 finality gates on a real lane:

1. New pools allow full finality only, so any block-depth request is rejected by the pool. The test first asserts the pool's default and expects the send to revert:

   ```solidity
   assertEq(TokenPool(sepoliaPool).getAllowedFinalityConfig(), FinalityCodec.WAIT_FOR_FINALITY_FLAG);
   vm.expectPartialRevert(FinalityCodec.InvalidRequestedFinality.selector);
   ```

2. Opt both pools in with `setAllowedFinalityConfig` (through the kit's `Example06SetPoolAllowedFinalityConfig` script), then find the smallest depth the live lane accepts by quoting `getFee` for candidate depths:

   ```solidity
   vm.selectFork(sepoliaFork);
   _setPoolMinBlockDepth(sepoliaPool, 1);
   uint16 depth = _findLaneFtfDepth(sepoliaToken);
   _setPoolMinBlockDepth(sepoliaPool, depth);
   vm.selectFork(amoyFork);
   _setPoolMinBlockDepth(amoyPool, depth);
   ```

3. Send with the custom finality (`blockConfirmations = depth`) and route. The transfer burns on the source and mints on the destination, same as the default-finality case, but delivered before full finality.

## What the fork simulator does not model

Not modelled by the simulator (and not asserted in the kit's fork tests): real CCV attestations, RMN and executor fees. CCVs on the lane are replaced by a synthetic verifier, and `executePendingV2Message` executes without charging the executor fee a real manual execution costs. Pinned state never sees testnet upgrades, so green tests only prove the examples against that snapshot; re-pin the fork blocks when the lane's behavior changes or on every `@chainlink/contracts-ccip` or `@chainlink/local` bump.

## Next steps

- The other fork tests cover Lock & Release pools with a lock box (`Example07.fork.t.sol`), `AdvancedPoolHooks` (`Example08`-`Example10`). For pool-required CCVs on `AdvancedPoolHooks`, read the [pool-based CCVs tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/pool-based-ccvs-fork).
- To fork mainnets, read [Using the Chainlink Local Simulator to fork mainnets](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/forking-mainnets).
- For the full CCT enabling procedure on the Sepolia → Amoy lane, read the [CCT burn and mint tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-burn-and-mint-fork) and the [CCT lock and release tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-lock-and-release-fork).
- For an index of every kit example and where its topic is documented, read the [CCIP starter kit examples map](/chainlink-local/learn/starter-kit-examples).
