# Using the Chainlink Local simulator in Remix IDE
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/build/ccip/remix/local-simulator

> **NOTE: Integrate Chainlink Local into your project**
>
> ### npm
>
> If you use [NPM](https://www.npmjs.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> npm install @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### yarn
>
> If you use [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/), install the [@chainlink/local NPM
> package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local):
>
> ```shell
> yarn add @chainlink/local@0.3.1
> ```
>
> ### foundry
>
> If you use [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/):
>
> ```shell
> forge install smartcontractkit/chainlink-local@v0.3.1
> ```
>
> and then set remappings to: `@chainlink/local/=lib/chainlink-local/` in either `remappings.txt` or `foundry.toml` file
>
> ### RemixIDE
>
> Import the `CCIPLocalSimulator` contract from the `@chainlink/local` package:
>
> ```solidity
> import {CCIPLocalSimulator} from "@chainlink/local@0.3.1/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulator.sol";
> ```

In this guide, you will test the [Chainlink CCIP getting started guide](/ccip/evm/getting-started) locally in Remix IDE. You will:

- Deploy a CCIP sender contract
- Deploy a CCIP receiver contract
- Use the local simulator to send data from the sender contract to the receiver contract

## Prerequisites

[Remix IDE](https://remix.ethereum.org/) is an online development environment that allows you to write, deploy, and test smart contracts. By default Remix IDE
does not persist the files that you open from an external source. To save files, you will need to manually create a workspace and copy the files into the workspace.

1. Open the [Remix IDE](https://remix.ethereum.org/) in your browser.

2. Create a [new workspace](https://remix-ide.readthedocs.io/en/latest/file_explorer.html#new-workspace).

3. Copy the content of the [Test Chainlink Local Simulator contract](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/documentation/blob/main/public/samples/CCIP/TestCCIPLocalSimulator.sol) into a new file in the workspace:

   ```sol
   // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   pragma solidity 0.8.24;

   // solhint-disable no-unused-import
   import {CCIPLocalSimulator} from "@chainlink/local/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulator.sol";
   ```

   When you compile, Remix resolves the `@chainlink/local`, `@chainlink/contracts-ccip`, and `@chainlink/contracts` imports from npm into the `.deps` folder. Without a version suffix, Remix uses the latest release of each package (`0.3.1` for `@chainlink/local`). To pin a specific version, use the version-suffixed form, for example `@chainlink/local@0.3.1/src/ccip/CCIPLocalSimulator.sol`.

4. Copy the content of the [Sender contract](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/documentation/blob/main/public/samples/CCIP/Sender.sol) into a new file in the workspace.

   ```sol
   // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   pragma solidity 0.8.24;

   import {IRouterClient} from "@chainlink/contracts-ccip/contracts/interfaces/IRouterClient.sol";
   import {Client} from "@chainlink/contracts-ccip/contracts/libraries/Client.sol";
   import {ExtraArgsCodec} from "@chainlink/contracts-ccip/contracts/libraries/ExtraArgsCodec.sol";
   import {OwnerIsCreator} from "@chainlink/contracts/src/v0.8/shared/access/OwnerIsCreator.sol";
   import {LinkTokenInterface} from "@chainlink/contracts/src/v0.8/shared/interfaces/LinkTokenInterface.sol";

   /**
    * THIS IS AN EXAMPLE CONTRACT THAT USES HARDCODED VALUES FOR CLARITY.
    * THIS IS AN EXAMPLE CONTRACT THAT USES UN-AUDITED CODE.
    * DO NOT USE THIS CODE IN PRODUCTION.
    */

   /// @title - A simple contract for sending string data across chains.
   contract Sender is OwnerIsCreator {
     error NotEnoughBalance(uint256 currentBalance, uint256 calculatedFees);

     event MessageSent(
       bytes32 indexed messageId,
       uint64 indexed destinationChainSelector,
       address receiver,
       string text,
       address feeToken,
       uint256 fees
     );

     IRouterClient private s_router;
     LinkTokenInterface private s_linkToken;

     /// @notice Constructor initializes the contract with the router address.
     /// @param _router The address of the router contract.
     /// @param _link The address of the LINK token contract.
     constructor(
       address _router,
       address _link
     ) {
       s_router = IRouterClient(_router);
       s_linkToken = LinkTokenInterface(_link);
     }

     /// @notice Sends data to receiver on the destination chain.
     /// @dev Assumes your contract has sufficient LINK to cover fees.
     /// @param destinationChainSelector The identifier (aka selector) for the destination blockchain.
     /// @param receiver The address of the recipient on the destination blockchain.
     /// @param text The string text to be sent.
     /// @return messageId The ID of the message that was sent.
     function sendMessage(
       uint64 destinationChainSelector,
       address receiver,
       string calldata text
     ) external onlyOwner returns (bytes32 messageId) {
       // Create an EVM2AnyMessage struct in memory with necessary information for sending a cross-chain message
       Client.EVM2AnyMessage memory evm2AnyMessage = Client.EVM2AnyMessage({
         receiver: abi.encode(receiver), // ABI-encoded receiver address
         data: abi.encode(text), // ABI-encoded string
         tokenAmounts: new Client.EVMTokenAmount[](0), // Empty array — no tokens are being sent
         extraArgs: ExtraArgsCodec._getBasicEncodedExtraArgsV3(
           200_000, // Gas limit for the callback on the destination chain
           bytes4(0) // Default finality (wait for full finalization)
         ),
         feeToken: address(s_linkToken) // Pay CCIP fees in LINK
       });

       // Get the fee required to send the message
       uint256 fees = s_router.getFee(destinationChainSelector, evm2AnyMessage);

       if (fees > s_linkToken.balanceOf(address(this))) {
         revert NotEnoughBalance(s_linkToken.balanceOf(address(this)), fees);
       }

       // Approve the Router to transfer LINK tokens on contract's behalf. It will spend the fees in LINK
       s_linkToken.approve(address(s_router), fees);

       // Send the message through the router and store the returned message ID
       messageId = s_router.ccipSend(destinationChainSelector, evm2AnyMessage);

       // Emit an event with message details
       emit MessageSent(messageId, destinationChainSelector, receiver, text, address(s_linkToken), fees);

       // Return the message ID
       return messageId;
     }
   }
   ```

5. Copy the content of the [Receiver contract](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/documentation/blob/main/public/samples/CCIP/Receiver.sol) into a new file in the workspace.

   ```sol
   // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
   pragma solidity 0.8.24;

   import {CCIPReceiver} from "@chainlink/contracts-ccip/contracts/applications/CCIPReceiver.sol";
   import {Client} from "@chainlink/contracts-ccip/contracts/libraries/Client.sol";
   import {FinalityCodec} from "@chainlink/contracts-ccip/contracts/libraries/FinalityCodec.sol";

   /**
    * THIS IS AN EXAMPLE CONTRACT THAT USES HARDCODED VALUES FOR CLARITY.
    * THIS IS AN EXAMPLE CONTRACT THAT USES UN-AUDITED CODE.
    * DO NOT USE THIS CODE IN PRODUCTION.
    */

   /// @title - A simple contract for receiving string data across chains.
   contract Receiver is CCIPReceiver {
     event MessageReceived(bytes32 indexed messageId, uint64 indexed sourceChainSelector, address sender, string text);

     bytes32 private s_lastReceivedMessageId;
     string private s_lastReceivedText;

     /// @notice Constructor initializes the contract with the router address.
     /// @param router The address of the router contract.
     constructor(
       address router
     ) CCIPReceiver(router) {}

     /// @notice Handle a received message.
     function _ccipReceive(
       Client.Any2EVMMessage memory any2EvmMessage
     ) internal override {
       s_lastReceivedMessageId = any2EvmMessage.messageId;
       s_lastReceivedText = abi.decode(any2EvmMessage.data, (string));

       emit MessageReceived(
         any2EvmMessage.messageId,
         any2EvmMessage.sourceChainSelector,
         abi.decode(any2EvmMessage.sender, (address)),
         abi.decode(any2EvmMessage.data, (string))
       );
     }

     /// @notice Returns the CCVs and finality config for a given source chain.
     /// @dev Override to advertise receiver finality policy to the OffRamp.
     function getCCVsAndFinalityConfig(
       uint64,
       bytes calldata
     )
       external
       view
       override
       returns (
         address[] memory requiredCCVs,
         address[] memory optionalCCVs,
         uint8 optionalThreshold,
         bytes4 allowedFinalityConfig
       )
     {
       return (new address[](0), new address[](0), 0, FinalityCodec.WAIT_FOR_FINALITY_FLAG);
     }

     /// @notice Fetches the details of the last received message.
     /// @return messageId The ID of the last received message.
     /// @return text The last received text.
     function getLastReceivedMessageDetails() external view returns (bytes32 messageId, string memory text) {
       return (s_lastReceivedMessageId, s_lastReceivedText);
     }
   }
   ```

At this point, you should have three files in your workspace:

- **TestCCIPLocalSimulator.sol**: The file imports the Chainlink Local simulator contract.

- **Sender.sol**: The file contains the Sender contract that interacts with CCIP to send data to the Receiver contract.

- **Receiver.sol**: The file contains the Receiver contract that receives data from the Sender contract.

## Deploy the contracts

1. Compile the contracts. In the Solidity Compiler tab, select version `0.8.24` to match the `pragma solidity 0.8.24` of the sample contracts.

2. Under the **Deploy & Run Transactions** tab, make sure *Remix VM* is selected in the **Environment** drop-down list. Remix will use a sandbox blockchain in the
   browser to deploy the contracts.

3. Deploy the [Chainlink Local simulator](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator#cciplocalsimulator):
   1. Select the `TestCCIPLocalSimulator.sol` file in the file explorer.
   2. In the *Contract* drop-down list, select `CCIPLocalSimulator`.
   3. Click the **Deploy** button.
   4. The `CCIPLocalSimulator` is shown in the **Deployed Contracts** section.
   5. In the list of functions, click the [`configuration`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator#configuration) function to retrieve the
      configuration details for the pre-deployed contracts and services needed for local CCIP simulations:

      ![Remix IDE Chainlink Local Simulator configuration](/images/chainlink-local/ccip/remix/cciplocalsimulator-configuration.jpg)

4. You will interact with the LINK token contract to fund the sender contract with LINK tokens. The LINK token contract is pre-deployed in the local simulator
   configuration, so you can load the LINK token contract instance:

   1. Select `LinkToken` in the *Contract* drop-down list.
   2. Fill in the *At Address* field with the address of the `LINK` token contract from the `CCIPLocalSimulator` configuration.
   3. Click the **At Address** button.

   The `LinkToken` contract is shown in the **Deployed Contracts** section.

5. Deploy the `Sender.sol` contract:

   1. Select the `Sender.sol` file in the file explorer.
   2. In the *Contract* drop-down list, select `Sender`.
   3. Under the *Deploy* section, fill in the constructor parameters:
      - `_router`: The address of the `sourceRouter` contract from the `CCIPLocalSimulator` configuration.
      - `_link`: The address of the `LINK` token contract from the `CCIPLocalSimulator` configuration.
   4. Click the **Deploy** button.

   The `Sender` contract is shown in the **Deployed Contracts** section.

6. Deploy the `Receiver.sol` contract:

   1. Select the `Receiver.sol` file in the file explorer.
   2. In the *Contract* drop-down list, select `Receiver`.
   3. Under the *Deploy* section, fill in the constructor parameters:
      - `_router`: The address of the `destinationRouter` contract from the `CCIPLocalSimulator` configuration.
   4. Click the **Deploy** button.

   The `Receiver` contract is shown in the **Deployed Contracts** section.

## Transfer data from the sender to the receiver

1. Fund the sender contract with LINK tokens to pay for CCIP fees:
   1. Copy the address of the `Sender` contract from the **Deployed Contracts** section.
   2. In the `CCIPLocalSimulator` contract, fill in the [`requestLinkFromFaucet`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator#requestlinkfromfaucet)
      function with the following inputs:
      - `to`: The address of the `Sender` contract.
      - `amount`: The amount of LINK tokens to transfer. For instance: 1000000000000000000.
   3. Click the **Transact** button.

2. Send data from the sender contract to the receiver contract:
   1. Copy the address of the `Receiver` contract from the **Deployed Contracts** section.

   2. In the `LinkToken` contract, call the `approve` function to let the `Sender` contract spend the LINK for the CCIP fee:
      - `spender`: The address of the `Sender` contract.
      - `value`: The amount of LINK to approve. For instance 1000000000000000000.

   3. In the `Sender` contract, fill in the `sendMessage` function with:
      - `destinationChainSelector`: The destination chain selector. You can find it in the `CCIPLocalSimulator` configuration.
      - `receiver`: The address of the `Receiver` contract.
      - `text`: The text to send. For instance Hello!.

   4. Remix IDE fails to estimate the gas properly for the `sendMessage` function. To work around this, you need to set the gas limit manually
      to 3000000:

      ![RemixIDE Chainlink Local sendMessage force gas limit](/images/chainlink-local/ccip/remix/sendMessage-estimateGas.jpg)

   5. Click the **Transact** button.

3. Check the receiver contract to verify the data transfer:
   1. In the `Receiver` contract, click on the `getLastReceivedMessageDetails` function.
   2. The `getLastReceivedMessageDetails` function returns the text sent from the `Sender` contract:

      ![RemixIDE Chainlink Local receivedMessage](/images/chainlink-local/ccip/remix/receivedMessage.jpg)

## Next steps

You have successfully tested the CCIP getting started guide within a few minutes using Remix IDE. Testing locally is useful to debug your contracts and fix any
issues before testing them on testnets, saving you time and resources. As an exercise, you can try any of the
[CCIP guides](/ccip/tutorials) using the local simulator in Remix IDE.

---

# Chainlink Local
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local

**Chainlink Local** is an installable package that allows you to run Chainlink services locally. You can import Chainlink Local into your preferred local development environment,
such as Foundry projects, Hardhat scripts, or the Remix IDE. Chainlink Local enables rapid exploration, prototyping, local development, and iteration with Chainlink services
before transitioning to a testnet.

For instance, you can use Chainlink Local to execute CCIP 2.0 token transfers and arbitrary messages on a local Hardhat or Anvil (Foundry) development node. Chainlink Local also supports forked nodes,
allowing you to work with multiple locally running blockchain networks using historical network states. User contracts tested with Chainlink Local can be deployed to test networks without modifications,
ensuring a seamless transition from local development to live testnets.

**Key Features of Chainlink Local:**

- **Local Simulation:** Run Chainlink services on a local development blockchain node, enabling fast and efficient testing and prototyping.
- **CCIP 2.0 rules in local mode:** The local router applies the CCIP 2.0 OnRamp and OffRamp message rules (finality, one token per message, receiver CCV config validation), so a test that passes locally does not fail on a fork or in production. See [CCIP 2.0 behavior in Chainlink Local](/chainlink-local/learn/ccip-v2-local).
- **Forked Networks:** Work with deployed Chainlink contracts using one or multiple forked networks, providing a more realistic testing environment. Fork routing supports every CCIP era: pre-1.6, 1.6 and CCIP 2.0 (CCV-based) lanes.
- **Seamless Integration:** Import the package into Foundry, Hardhat 3, or Remix IDE projects without modifying your contracts for local testing.

> **NOTE: Hardhat 2 users**
>
> Chainlink Local `0.3.x` (V3) does not compile under Hardhat 2. Hardhat 2 users stay on the `0.2.x` line (`npm install
>   @chainlink/local@0.2.9`), which supports pre-1.6 fork routing only.

To get started testing CCIP with Chainlink Local, follow the installation and setup steps in the CCIP guides for [Foundry](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry), [Hardhat](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/hardhat), or [Remix IDE](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/remix). For an index of every CCIP starter kit example and where its topic is documented, read the [CCIP starter kit examples map](/chainlink-local/learn/starter-kit-examples).

---

# Chainlink Local Architecture
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/learn/architecture

[Chainlink Local](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-local) is a package that you can import into your development environment
(such as Hardhat, Foundry, or Remix IDE) to use Chainlink services locally. It supports two primary modes:

- Local testing without forking.
- Local testing with forking.

This enables you to test Chainlink smart contracts and services, such as CCIP, either in a clean local blockchain state or by using a forked state from a live blockchain.

After testing with Chainlink Local, you can deploy your contracts to test networks without any modifications.

## Local testing without forking

In this mode, you work with mock contracts on a locally running development blockchain node, such as Hardhat, Anvil (Foundry), or Remix VM.

**How it works**: Import the [Chainlink Local](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chainlink/local) package and deploy a set of Chainlink smart contracts to a blank Hardhat/Anvil network EVM state as part of your tests.
You can then deploy your smart contracts and start testing with them. For CCIP, the local router applies the CCIP 2.0 OnRamp and OffRamp message rules, so a test that passes locally does not fail on a fork or in production. Read [CCIP 2.0 behavior in Chainlink Local](/chainlink-local/learn/ccip-v2-local) for what is and is not enforced.

![Chainlink Local Architecture (Without Forking)](/images/chainlink-local/chainlink-local-no-fork.png)

## Local testing with forking

In this mode, you work with deployed Chainlink smart contracts using one or more forked blockchains. This setup provides a more realistic testing environment by incorporating
the state of a live blockchain.

> **NOTE: Supported Development environments**
>
> Chainlink Local does not support forking with Remix IDE. Forking is currently supported only for Hardhat and Foundry.

**How it works**: In your test scripts, you fork one or more blockchains to create locally running blockchain network(s). Chainlink Local provides the necessary interfaces
to interact with the forked Chainlink services and utilities for testing in a forked environment. For example, in CCIP, Chainlink Local provides a utility function that helps
you switch from one fork (as the source chain) to another fork (as the destination chain). Fork routing supports every CCIP era: pre-1.6, 1.6 and CCIP 2.0 (CCV-based) lanes, which live testnet lanes run today. Read [CCIP 2.0 behavior in Chainlink Local](/chainlink-local/learn/ccip-v2-local) for the fork-mode details.

![Chainlink Local Architecture (With Forking)](/images/chainlink-local/chainlink-local-fork.png)

---

# CCIP 2.0 behavior in Chainlink Local
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/learn/ccip-v2-local

Chainlink Local `v0.3.x` (V3) targets CCIP 2.0: it pins `@chainlink/contracts-ccip` 2.0.0, and both the local-mode router and the fork simulator apply the CCIP 2.0 message rules. This page describes what those rules are in each mode, so you know what a passing local test proves before you move to a fork or a live lane.

Read the [CCIP 2.0 concepts](/ccip/evm/concepts/best-practices) for the protocol itself; this page covers only the Chainlink Local behavior.

## Local mode (no fork)

`CCIPLocalSimulator` deploys a [`CCIPLocalRouter`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-router) that delivers messages synchronously inside `ccipSend`. The router mirrors `MockCCIPRouter` from `@chainlink/contracts-ccip` 2.0.0 (same ABI, events and behaviour) and additionally applies the CCIP 2.0 OnRamp and OffRamp message rules, so a test that passes locally does not fail on a fork or in production.

### Enforced at send time

- **Finality**: the requested finality of `ExtraArgsV3` must use a single mode (the OnRamp check). A Faster-Than-Finality message that is not a token-only transfer is only delivered to a receiver whose `getCCVsAndFinalityConfig` allows the requested finality (the OffRamp check). Receivers without `IAny2EVMMessageReceiverV2` accept finalized messages only.
- **One token per message**: more than one token in `tokenAmounts` reverts with `CanOnlySendOneTokenPerMessage`.
- **No zero amounts**: a zero-amount token reverts with `CannotSendZeroTokens`.
- **No V3 `tokenReceiver` on EVM lanes**: `GenericExtraArgsV3.tokenReceiver` reverts with `TokenReceiverNotAllowed`.
- **Receiver CCV config validation**: duplicate required/optional CCVs and `optionalThreshold > optionalCCVs.length` are rejected the same way the OffRamp rejects them.
- **Gas limit**: only V1/V2 extraArgs gas limits above `uint32` revert `MessageGasLimitTooHigh`. Local mode has no lane config, so lower lane caps are not enforced.

### Not simulated in local mode

- **Token pools**: pool finality policies, rate limits and pool-required CCVs are not enforced; tokens go directly to the receiver.
- **CCVs and block confirmations**: receiver CCV lists are validated, not verified. There are no CCV verifiers, so no quorum check happens.
- **The supported-token list**: `getSupportedTokens` is informational.
- **Manual execution**: `NO_EXECUTION_ADDRESS` messages are executed immediately.
- **The lane's `maxPerMsgGasLimit`**: only the `uint32` ceiling above is enforced.

Use fork mode to test these against the real contracts.

### Fees and message IDs

The local router charges only what `router.setFee(...)` sets (default 0), in the fee token you choose (native or LINK). It returns a mock message ID that is not calculated from the message contents the way a real message ID is, so the `CCIPMessageSent` event some tools look for is never emitted locally.

## Fork mode

`CCIPLocalSimulatorFork` (Foundry) and the Hardhat 3 JavaScript helper route messages on forked networks for every CCIP era: pre-1.6 (`EVM2EVMOnRamp`), 1.6 and CCIP 2.0 (CCV-based lanes, which live testnet lanes run today).

### CCIP 2.0 routing

On CCIP 2.0 lanes the destination OffRamp selects the CCVs and executes the message. The default `V2VerificationMode` is `OFFRAMP_DERIVED`: the CCV selection is derived from the destination OffRamp's `getCCVsForMessage(encodedMessage)` and the raw encoded message is executed through the permissionless `execute` entrypoint, so routing does not depend on the local `MessageV1` codec. CCV attestations are simulated with a synthetic no-op verifier.

Fast Transfer messages with data are only delivered to receivers that opt in through `getCCVsAndFinalityConfig`, as in production.

### Strict routing and message status

Routing is strict by default: `switchChainAndRouteMessage` reverts with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork__MessageNotRouted(messageId, reason)` when a captured message cannot be routed to any of the given forks, and with `CCIPLocalSimulatorFork__MessageExecutionFailed(messageId, reason)` (the decoded revert data) when it does not execute successfully. Call `setStrictRouting(false)` to record failures instead and read them with `getMessageStatus(messageId)`, which returns `NOT_FOUND`, `QUEUED`, `FAILED` or `SUCCESS`.

With several destinations, either pass every destination fork at once with the `uint256[] forkIds` overload, or call `switchChainAndRouteMessage` once per destination fork: a 1.6 or 2.0 message to a chain that is not in the call stays `QUEUED` and is routed by the call that includes its destination fork.

### CCIP 2.0 routers

Some chains have a dedicated CCIP 2.0 router deployed next to the router that `getNetworkDetails` returns (the `Register` is generated from the CCIP docs API and only carries one router per chain). Read it with `getCCIPV2RouterAddress(chainId)` (Ethereum Sepolia and Avalanche Fuji are pre-registered) or set it with `setCCIPV2RouterAddress`. Send through the CCIP 2.0 router to use its CCIP 2.0 lanes; messages sent through either router are routed by `switchChainAndRouteMessage`.

### Manual execution

`NO_EXECUTION_ADDRESS` messages follow the CCIP 2.0 manual execution path: with the default `V2ExecutionMode.RESPECT_NO_EXEC`, they are queued instead of executed. List them with `getPendingV2MessageIds` and execute one with `executePendingV2Message(messageId)`.

### Not simulated in fork mode

Real CCV attestations, RMN and executor fees are not modelled; CCVs on the lane are replaced by a synthetic verifier, and `executePendingV2Message` executes without charging the executor fee a real manual execution costs. Pinned fork state never sees testnet upgrades, so green tests only prove your code against that snapshot.

## Requirements

- Fork tests need `evm_version = "cancun"` or later (deployed CCIP 2.0 contracts use Cancun opcodes; `paris` fails with `EvmError: NotActivated`) and Foundry >= 1.5.1.
- Hardhat 3 (Node.js 22) is required for the JavaScript fork helper; Hardhat 2 is not supported in `0.3.x` (the contracts do not compile, `HH411`). Hardhat 2 users stay on `0.2.x` (`npm install @chainlink/local@0.2.9`), which supports pre-1.6 fork routing only.

# Contributing to Chainlink Local
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/learn/contributing

Contributions to Chainlink Local are welcome! These contributions can include bug fixes, new features, and documentation updates. This guide provides a list of repositories you can contribute to:

- [Chainlink Local](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-local): The main repository for Chainlink Local.
- [CCIP Foundry Starter Kit](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry): A Foundry starter kit for Chainlink CCIP. It uses Chainlink Local test different scenarios on a local environment with and without forking.
- [CCIP Hardhat Starter Kit](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-hardhat): A Hardhat starter kit for Chainlink CCIP. It uses Chainlink Local test different scenarios on a local environment with and without forking.
- [Chainlink Technical Documentation](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/documentation): You are welcome to write new guides or update existing guides in the Chainlink documentation.

# CCIP starter kit examples map
Source: https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-local/learn/starter-kit-examples

The [CCIP starter kits](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry) ([Foundry](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-foundry) and [Hardhat 3](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/ccip-starter-kit-hardhat)) teach CCIP 2.0 through examples `Example01`-`Example10` plus two legacy examples, each with a chapter in the kit's own book and a test that runs against Chainlink Local. This page maps every example to what it teaches, its kit book chapter, and the docs.chain.link page that covers the same topic, so you can find where each feature is documented.

The kits pin Chainlink Local `v0.3.1`, `@chainlink/contracts-ccip` 2.0.0 and `solc 0.8.26` with `evm_version = cancun`. Examples 01-10 use Ethereum Sepolia → Polygon Amoy as their primary CCIP 2.0 lane.

## Local mode examples (Example01-Example05)

These tests run against the no-fork [`CCIPLocalSimulator`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator): no RPC URLs needed, messages delivered synchronously inside `ccipSend`, with the CCIP 2.0 OnRamp and OffRamp message rules applied. Read [CCIP 2.0 behavior in local mode](/chainlink-local/learn/ccip-v2-local) for what is enforced.

| Example                                            | What it teaches                                                                                      | Chainlink Local guide                                                                                                                                               | Related CCIP docs                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 01 - Token Transfer + Fast Transfers               | Token-only transfer to an EOA with `ExtraArgsV3` and non-zero block confirmations                    | [Foundry](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/local-simulator) · [Hardhat](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/hardhat/local-simulator)                                     | [Transfer tokens from a contract](/ccip/evm/tutorials/application-developers/transfer-tokens-from-contract) |
| 02 - Hello World to `BasicMessageReceiverWithCCVs` | Data-only message to a receiver with CCV config; the receiver's `minBlockDepth` gates Fast Transfers | [Foundry](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/data-messages-receiver-ccv-config) · [Hardhat](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/hardhat/data-messages-receiver-ccv-config) | [Send arbitrary data](/ccip/evm/tutorials/application-developers/send-arbitrary-data)                       |
| 03 - Programmable Token Transfer (Fast Transfers)  | Data + tokens in one message to a contract receiver, with the receiver finality gate                 | Kit book chapter                                                                                                                                                    | [Programmable token transfers](/ccip/evm/tutorials/application-developers/programmable-token-transfers)     |
| 04 - Programmable Token Transfer (sender contract) | Same transfer through a `BasicMessageSender` contract with default finality                          | Kit book chapter                                                                                                                                                    | [Programmable token transfers](/ccip/evm/tutorials/application-developers/programmable-token-transfers)     |
| 05 - ExtraArgsV3 no-execution tag                  | The `NO_EXECUTION_ADDRESS` executor for the manual execution path                                    | Kit book chapter                                                                                                                                                    | [Manual execution](/ccip/evm/tutorials/application-developers/manual-execution)                             |

Local mode does not model executors or manual execution: `NO_EXECUTION_ADDRESS` messages are executed immediately, so Example 05's test only verifies what the script sends. Whether the message stays pending until manually executed can only be observed on a real lane or a fork.

## Fork mode examples (Example06-Example10)

These tests run against pinned forks of Ethereum Sepolia and Polygon Amoy through [`CCIPLocalSimulatorFork`](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork) (Foundry) or the [Hardhat 3 JavaScript fork helper](/chainlink-local/api-reference/v0.3.1/ccip-local-simulator-fork-js). They need archive-capable RPC URLs and, in Foundry, `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=fork`. Read [CCIP 2.0 behavior in fork mode](/chainlink-local/learn/ccip-v2-local) for what is simulated.

| Example                                         | What it teaches                                                                                                   | Chainlink Local guide                                                                                                                                             | Related CCIP docs                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 06 - CCT Burn and Mint                          | `CrossChainToken` + BurnMint pool deployment, TokenAdminRegistry registration, lane linking, pool finality config | [CCT burn and mint tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-burn-and-mint-fork) · [fork guide](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/local-simulator-fork) | [Register a Burn and Mint token from an EOA](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-foundry)      |
| 07 - CCT Lock and Release                       | `CrossChainToken` + `ERC20LockBox` + LockRelease pool, destination lock box liquidity                             | [CCT lock and release tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/cct-lock-and-release-fork)                                                                    | [Register a Lock and Mint token from an EOA](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-foundry)      |
| 08 - CCT Burn and Mint with `AdvancedPoolHooks` | Attaching a pool hook with a sender allowlist and CCV threshold                                                   | Kit book chapter                                                                                                                                                  | [Configure a sender allowlist](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/configure-sender-allowlist-advanced-pool-hooks-foundry) |
| 09 - Pool-based CCVs on `AdvancedPoolHooks`     | Pool-required CCVs consulted outbound by the OnRamp and verified inbound by the OffRamp; threshold CCVs           | [Pool-based CCVs tutorial](/chainlink-local/build/ccip/foundry/pool-based-ccvs-fork)                                                                              | [CCV starter kit](https://docs.chain.link/ccip/ccv-starter-kit)                                                               |
| 10 - Policy engine on `AdvancedPoolHooks`       | An ACE policy engine attached to the hook, capping transfer amounts                                               | Kit book chapter                                                                                                                                                  | [Enforce ACE policies](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/enforce-ace-policies-foundry)                                   |

Pool-required CCVs (Example 09) are the one CCIP 2.0 feature local mode cannot exercise: local mode has no token pools, so pool-required CCVs are not enforced there. Only the fork tests run them against the real OnRamp and OffRamp.

## Legacy examples

| Example                                | What it teaches                                                                       | Related CCIP docs                                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Legacy 01 - ExtraArgsV1 token transfer | The v1.x `EVMExtraArgsV1` format on an older lane                                     | [Using `extraArgs`](/ccip/evm/concepts/best-practices#using-extraargs) |
| Legacy 02 - ExtraArgsV2 token transfer | The `GenericExtraArgsV2` format; `allowOutOfOrderExecution` is deprecated in CCIP 2.0 | [Using `extraArgs`](/ccip/evm/concepts/best-practices#using-extraargs) |

## Kit books and tools

Each kit ships an mdBook with one chapter per example, including the exact script and task commands for live-testnet runs:

- [Foundry kit book](https://smartcontractkit.github.io/ccip-starter-kit-foundry/)
- [Hardhat kit book](https://smartcontractkit.github.io/ccip-starter-kit-hardhat/)

The books also cover the CCIP API, the CCIP SDK (`ccip-send`, `ccip-track`) and the CCIP CLI, which are not Chainlink Local features.
